method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the rules are applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (the text's no where it says no; NOTHING, or an answer marked NOTHING-kind, where it does not answer); the dates in one module, the rules and exported questions in another, the cases in a third; two regulative rules (the defendant's defence within the r 102 / r 111 time; the offeror's payment within 28 days after acceptance) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Court Procedures Rules 2006 (ACT), SL2006-29, Republication No 73 (R73), effective 1 August 2026, last amended by SL2026-11, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/SL2006-29.txt; schedules 2 and 3 of the same republication
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the quoted text is (c) Australian Capital Territory, used under CC BY 4.0; see SOURCE-LICENSE.md
seat: the person bringing a claim (the plaintiff): the injured person, the family of a person who died, or the creditor who brings a civil claim in the ACT Supreme Court or Magistrates Court (cpr-claims.l4)
focus: the provisions a claimant meets: starting and keeping the proceeding alive, the defendant's time to defend and default, offers of compromise and their costs, interest up to and after judgment, fixed costs, small-win costs in the Supreme Court, and who may bring a death claim

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run cpr-dates.l4 ; l4 run cpr-claims.l4 ; l4 run cpr-cases.l4
checks.result: 182 assertions written, 182 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07, after the verification fixes); a deliberately wrong expected day in a scratch copy showed as 3 failed
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: In: r 32 with r 74 (6), r 76 (5); r 74; r 75 with r 76 (3); r 55; r 102 (1); r 111 (3)-(5); r 1116, r 1117, r 1118 (1), r 1120-r 1126; r 1101, r 1102 and sch 3 pt 3.1; r 1121 and sch 3 pt 3.2; r 1725; Part 2.10 (r 1001, r 1002 (5), (6), (9), r 1003 (1), r 1004 (1), r 1009-r 1014); r 1619 (7), (8); r 1620 (1), (2); sch 2; r 250; r 6350 (3). Out: the rest of the rules (content of process, pleadings, disclosure, evidence, trial, the rest of costs and interest, enforcement, Chapter 3 including Part 3.13 workers compensation arbitrations, Chapters 4-7). Reasons in NOTES.md.
also_reads: subjects/au/act/limitation-act-1985 (the time limits a proceeding's start day is measured against)
subjects/au/act/workers-compensation-act-1951 (Part 3.13 of these rules governs its arbitrations; not encoded here)
subjects/au/act/civil-law-wrongs-act-2002 (part 3.1 death claims, ch 14 costs limits to which Part 2.10 is subject)
